clue.text: Last month I live beside Lake — the level of noise

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, shortened to DEC
to live is to be, exist
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone living by a lake at the end of the year notes how loud it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit used to measure loudness, so the word stands for a reading of sound intensity.

clue.text: Openings to develop economic confidence — a politician has to sneak away

indicators.note: the openings of these three words are their first letters, taken in turn

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Kickstarting growth and confidence, a politician still slips off quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave suddenly or secretly, often to avoid trouble, is the verb's usual sense.

clue.text: Church vessels, containers of milk?

parts.note: urns are vessels, large pots

explanation.surface: A question about the pots used in churches and whether they hold milk.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on churns as large metal cans for carrying milk from farms; the question mark flags the indirect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk churns are the large cans that dairy farms traditionally used to carry milk.

clue.text: Child-minder disgruntled about area beside front of sofa

indicators.note: the word for disgruntled goes around the other pieces

parts.note: someone disgruntled feels resentful, bitter
by means next to, beside

indicators.note: the front of the word sofa is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grumpy carer sits next to the sofa sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgruntled' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is simply a synonym; 'about' then wraps that word around the area, beside and sofa pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person paid to look after children while parents are out is a child-minder.

clue.text: Bar in wild party getting overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a revel is a noisy, lively celebration

explanation.surface: Things get knocked over in a pub during a rowdy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to match the party, but it means a metal rod used to prise.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar or rigid rod used to prise things up is a simple machine of this name.

clue.text: Figure page will display part of plant

parts.note: FIG is the abbreviation for figure, as in an illustration in a book
a leaf is a page of a book

explanation.surface: A book's illustration on one page shows a piece of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a leaf of the fig tree, which is a part of a plant.

clue.text: Sack with flour, perhaps, daughter dropped — how much damage could be done?

definitions.text: how much damage could be done?

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job

indicators.note: the letter for daughter is dropped from the word for flour's kind

parts.note: flour is an example of a powder
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A baker wonders what harm a bag of flour could do once a girl knocked it over.
explanation.definitionFit: The destructive capacity of weapons or an army is measured as its strength in shooting.

clue.text: Information about loch and valley

indicators.note: the word for information goes round the letter for loch

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is an abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Gathering facts about a Scottish lake and the land around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow valley, especially in Scotland, is the Scots word for such a dale.

clue.text: Motto for book, no end of a long story and plot

indicators.note: the long story loses its final letter

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative tale
to plot data is to graph it

explanation.surface: Choosing a motto for a book with an endless saga and plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quotation at the start of a book or chapter, setting its theme, is an epigraph.

clue.text: Sole business for a dab hand?

definitions.text: Sole business for a dab hand?

parts.words: Sole business for a dab hand?
parts.note: sole and dab are both flatfish, so the business that rears them suits a dab hand in a second sense

explanation.surface: Asking whether an expert should have one single business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' reads as only and 'dab hand' as an expert, but both are fish names, pointing to a farm that raises fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquaculture business where fish such as sole are bred commercially for food.

clue.text: Small piece in Czech's beginning odd book

indicators.note: the beginning of Czech's is its first letter

parts.note: rum means odd, peculiar, in British slang

explanation.surface: Something tiny turns up at the start of a strange Czech book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment, especially of bread or cake, is a crumb.

clue.text: Very first zodiac sign includes obligation for different types

indicators.note: the zodiac sign holds the word for obligation inside it

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac
a tie is a bond or obligation

explanation.surface: An astrologer notes that the very first star sign comes with duties of different kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds or sorts of something are its varieties, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Wild turnip scam presented in document

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy fraud involving a turnip is written up in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten or typed text, such as an author's draft, is a manuscript.

clue.text: Academic supporting French

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

explanation.surface: A scholar who backs the French side.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for professor, an informal name for a university teacher.

clue.text: New Orleans — his for the most part

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A city name, New Orleans, is claimed by someone as largely his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city, but 'New' is the anagram signal working on ORLEANS and HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest portion of something, from the fable where the lion takes everything, is an idiom.

clue.text: Something overheard: 'Small white grapes crushed'

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

indicators.note: crushed grapes are mashed up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snippet of gossip about small white grapes being pressed for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's loud aside meant to be heard by the audience, though supposedly private, is an overheard remark.

clue.text: Beginning to gabble, pronouncing 'rain run-offs'

indicators.note: the beginning of gabble is its first letter

parts.note: uttering is saying aloud, pronouncing words

explanation.surface: Someone starts to babble while saying the phrase rain run-offs.
explanation.definitionFit: The channels along a roof edge that carry rainwater away are collectively called guttering.

clue.text: Excellent — installing central heating always a success

indicators.note: the word for excellent has central heating fitted inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, excellent, written here as the letters AI
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating in property ads
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A heating engineer boasts that a first-rate central heating installation always works.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as letters A and I, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who succeeds and reaches goals is a success, a high-performing person.

clue.text: One with common sense circumvents family of ill-repute

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for common sense goes around the short form of family

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence, common sense
fam is an informal shortening of family

explanation.surface: A sensible person bypasses a family with a bad reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Well known for something bad, notorious, which is what having ill repute means.

clue.text: Church's initial organ trend disrupted around introduction of cool piano

indicators.note: the initial of Church's is its first letter
the rearranged letters wrap around the first letter of cool
disrupted signals that organ and trend are thrown into a new order
the introduction of cool is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A church organist notices a changing fashion in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests church music, but it is anagram fodder: 'disrupted' rearranges it with trend, and 'around' wraps that mix round the first letter of cool.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest kind of grand piano, built for concert halls, is a specific type of piano.

clue.text: Explorer on screen found under iron hat

indicators.note: in a down clue the explorer's name sits below the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora the Explorer is a children's TV cartoon character

explanation.surface: A screen adventurer turns up beneath an iron hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim is a type of headwear.

clue.text: Mean and causing some pain?

definitions.meaning: mean as in tight-fisted, unwilling to spend
playfully, something that stings is sting-y, giving a sting

explanation.definitionFit: Ungenerous with money is the usual sense; read literally it means having a sting.

clue.text: Tablet computer father identified in documents

indicators.note: the word for father is placed inside the abbreviation for documents

parts.note: ID is short for identity documents
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad's tablet computer is listed among his papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's tablet computer, a brand name widely used for tablets.

clue.text: Not giving up modifying prettiness

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so the letters of the next word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on tweaking their good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing firmly despite difficulty is being dogged, refusing to quit.

clue.text: Position is inverted in this form of exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue the two words are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: to position something is to put it

explanation.surface: Lying upside down as part of a workout routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An abdominal exercise where you raise your torso from lying flat is a gym move.

clue.text: Partner reduced current internet access?

indicators.note: the word for partner is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a wife is a marriage partner
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A spouse cuts back on the electricity bill for getting online.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless networking that connects devices to the internet without cables.

clue.text: Leader, perhaps — hence bowing and scraping?

definitions.text: Leader, perhaps — hence bowing and scraping?

parts.words: Leader, perhaps — hence bowing and scraping?
parts.note: the leader of an orchestra is its first violin, who bows the strings and scrapes them, not someone fawning

explanation.surface: A leader is surrounded by servile flatterers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowing and scraping' suggests grovelling to a boss, but it is literally how a string player works the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the violin; the leader of an orchestra is its principal violin player.

clue.text: A swindle involving Republican — source of greater things later?

indicators.note: the swindle wraps around the abbreviation for Republican

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a trick
R is short for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A fraud involving a Republican politician hints at bigger things to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying that great oaks from little acorns grow.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed from which a huge oak tree grows, hence a small beginning of something big.

clue.text: Parisian is into boxing, not working in the theatre

indicators.note: the French word is put into the word for a boxing venue

parts.note: a ring is where boxing takes place
est is the French for is, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A French boxer is out of work as an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Out-of-work actors are traditionally described as resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical euphemism for an actor between jobs, temporarily unemployed.

clue.text: Revised reply about article rejected in full assembly

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the turned-back article
revised signals the letters of reply are reworked
rejected means sent back, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A revised response about a rejected article is presented to the whole assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges reply, and 'about' wraps those letters around the article turned back by 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting attended by all members, a full session of a body, is a plenary.
